Your exploratory data analysis of the team datasets go here.

Dataset: https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/blob/main/data/2024/2024-05-14/readme.md

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(here)
library(fs)
coffee_survey <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2024/2024-05-14/coffee_survey.csv')

head(coffee_survey)
```
>Used this to view the data and we can see there are a lot of NA values so we need to specify what we are looking at. 

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# Create a small, focused dataset for your analysis
cups_summary <- coffee_survey |>
  select(age, cups, where_drink) |>
  drop_na()
head(cups_summary)
```
>Specifed the criteria that we would look at. From this we were able to see the relationship between coffee preferances and age. 

```{r}
cups_summary <- coffee_survey |>
  select(age, where_drink, favorite) |>
  drop_na()
head(cups_summary)
```
>Continued to specify the criteria that we would look at. From this we were able to see the relationship between other coffee preferances and age. 

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# Load the dataset directly from GitHub
coffee_survey <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2024/2024-05-14/coffee_survey.csv")

top_reasons <- coffee_survey |>
  filter(!is.na(why_drink)) |>
  separate_rows(why_drink, sep = ",\\s*") |>
  count(why_drink, sort = TRUE) |>
  mutate(pct_of_respondents = round(n / sum(!is.na(coffee_survey$why_drink)) * 100, 1))

print(top_reasons)
```
>Attempted to see if there is any relationships between age and reasons for drinking coffee.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

coffee_survey <- read_csv("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2024/2024-05-14/coffee_survey.csv")

coffee_survey |>
  filter(!is.na(why_drink)) |>
  # Standardize order of reasons inside each string so "A, B" and "B, A" match
  mutate(
    combo = map_chr(str_split(why_drink, ",\\s*"), ~ paste(sort(.x), collapse = " + "))
  ) |>
  count(combo, sort = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 10) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y = reorder(combo, n))) +
  geom_col(fill = "#6F4E37", width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), hjust = -0.2, size = 3.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(
    title = "Top 10 Combinations of Reasons People Drink Coffee",
    x = "Number of Respondents",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
